It does not close lane-b-ask-ai-ext (no variants or contextChecks). fault-stack.sh starts a private backend on 5330/5331 from a scratch copy and refuses without QA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENV=1. 'NEW TODAY' on H3 and HX (added today by the server's day) shows in A and is missing in B and B2. Day/visit numbers: absent in every context (judged in S26/S06). Known and worse: such a device also rolls New Admission / Consult to Follow-up on the server for every device (TFA-92584 AC 8).

Nursing Home (API): pass — get null, no row names the id in any patient-linked table, audit for the patient = before + 1 delete row with the earlier PHI_READ kept, control unchanged. Hospital (API and card trash icon -> OK): chart, list projection and every other table clean, audit trail correct, control unchanged, BUT the Quick Dictation compartment placed on the deleted patient survives: quickDictationDrafts row with assignedPatientId = the deleted id, assignedLabel '412 · QA Hosp Del Target …', and the dictated text; the Quick Dictation screen after the delete still lists '412 · QA Hosp Del Target …' with Dictate / Re-assign. The confirm dialog read: 'Remove <name> from the rounding list? This will delete all notes, vitals, and encounter data for this patient.'
Product issue: After a physician deletes a Hospital patient (trash icon -> OK), opening Quick Dictation still shows a compartment labelled with the deleted patient's room and full name ('412 · <name>') holding what was dictated for them; the stored quickDictationDrafts row still points at the deleted chart. Overlaps TC-24 Q6(a) (whether the compartment and its 'room · name' label must go) and is already listed in the TC-24 risks.

Re-run 16:58–17:00 with --repeat-each=3 and evidence per repeat (…-rep<N>.json), plus a slow-link variant at 17:29. (a) Two ticks with no wait between the clicks (measured gap 0 ms; both clicks done within ~70 ms): the first tick is lost 6/6 (Hospital 'Repeat BMP in the morning', NH 'Recheck INR Friday' open in the store and on screen after reload). Same two ticks 400 ms apart on localhost (measured 403–405 ms): both stick 6/6. Same 400 ms gap over a 500 ms round trip (every sync-socket message delayed 250 ms each way, as on weak hospital cellular): the first tick is lost 6/6. (b) Another writer (API, the physician's JWT) adds a task, then a different task is ticked: ticked 13–30 ms after the write, the added task ('Follow up blood cultures' / 'Repeat CBC next week') is lost 5/6 (Hospital rep1, rep2; NH rep0–2; Hospital rep0 kept it); ticked after the added task shows (57–117 ms), both survive 6/6. The earlier run's unsuffixed files are kept under evidence/tc07-s27/_earlier-run-unsuffixed (one of them came from a passing repeat).
Product issue: On Task Export (both modes), a second tick made before the first tick's write has come back from the server undoes the first: the task the physician ticked is open again after reload. On a good connection this needs two taps within the round trip (localhost: lost with no gap, kept 6/6 at 400 ms), but over a 500 ms round trip two ticks 400 ms apart lose the first one 6/6. Likewise a task added from another tab or device is dropped if the physician ticks a different task before the new task has appeared on this screen (lost 5/6 at 13–30 ms after the write; kept 6/6 once it shows). Breaks TC-07 U1/U2 (no open task lost, no completed task reverted). Cause: TasksOverlay.onToggleTask writes the whole tasks array built from the rendered list (patch {tasks: newTasks}) with no optimistic update.

NH: going offline inside the 800 ms autosave keeps a device copy (one put, no delete); (b) F is restored on the phone and reaches the computer, draft row gone after the echo; (a) the computer's later G wins and F is dropped silently (record-only, Q11). Hospital: the probe (every put/delete on the draft store, init script) shows the copy IS written with a valid key while offline (so the session / draftId is not null) and deleted 4–7 ms later, still offline, while the server never had F; after the page closes F is gone: (b) neither the phone, the computer nor the server has it; (a) G shown, F gone. Cause, from the probe + code: Hospital saves through rounding.update with an optimistic update (src/routes/rounding/Patient.tsx:33) that patches the local chart at once, so useAutosave's 'server echoed my text' check (src/lib/useAutosave.ts:101-110) fires locally and deletes the copy before anything reached the server; Nursing Home saves without one and keeps the copy. That path is local and does not depend on how the network is cut, so it should hold on a real phone in airplane mode — still worth one device check.

The device copy is written and then deleted at once by the local optimistic echo (Patient.tsx:33 + useAutosave.ts:101-110), before the server has the text. Breaks Empty & Failure States 'nothing typed is lost' (TC-25 S28 b).

Neither display window reads the retention config. In the Hospital timeline, isRecentCourseLine (apps/web/src/domain/courseTimeline.ts:62-68) keeps a dated line only if its label equals today's or yesterday's date (todayCourseLabel / yesterdayCourseLabel). The two-day window is fixed in client code. In the Nursing Home course panel, CoursePanel.tsx:12 sets its own `const SHOW_LAST = 3`. HOSPITAL_RETENTION and SNF_RETENTION in convex/lib/lifecycle.ts are module-private (`const`, not exported) and are used only by the backend purge. SNF_RETENTION does set transcriptVisits: 3, which happens to match SHOW_LAST, but the panel never reads it. So lengthening retention under a hospital affiliation would change what the purge keeps but not what either timeline shows. This goes against UAT 3.6 ("all windows are configuration values"). The oracle says such a window is a finding that becomes a Fail or a pass only once Q15 decides whether the displayed window must follow the config. Both findings are therefore labelled pending:Q15 and the verdict is pending. No recorded gap applies.

The browser then POSTs its SDP offer to https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls with that secret, and the audio goes straight to OpenAI over WebRTC. (2) 'gpt-live', recovery of a kept recording: the recording is uploaded to the authenticated `transcribeAudio` action, which sends it to whisper-1 at https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions from the server. Neither context calls an EHR. Both Post-Round tabs send Copy to EMR through useCopyToEmr, and that calls only copyTextToClipboard: the Capacitor Clipboard on mobile, otherwise navigator.clipboard.writeText, with a hidden-textarea execCommand fallback. A grep of apps/web/src and apps/web/convex for FHIR, HL7, Epic, Cerner, SMART or "EHR" as a whole word finds nothing. In both contexts, marking the encounter complete only saves the app's own record (status set to post-rounded or complete) and writes a usage-analytics row. The Nursing Home tab calls useCopyToEmr(ex.note || "") with no callback, and the file never imports useLogExport, so copying a Nursing Home note writes no export record. The rule says a context without the export record fails. This is a new gap that waits on no open question, so the verdict is fail. I found no "Copy A&P" control in either Post-Round tab, so there was nothing to review for it. code-review: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane wrote no productIssue; counted from its physicianImpact))
Two parts of U6 pass and one fails. First, Haiku and Mistral both go through the same invoke. chat() builds the request once (bedrockRequest) and sends both the primary and the fallback through internal.ai.providers.bedrock.invoke. That function adds one guardrailConfig built from the environment (BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID / BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION), so both models get the same guardrail id and version. Second, the IAM policy has a Deny rule (DenyInvokeWithoutGuardrail) on InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream whenever bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier is missing. The version, though, is not pinned, so U6 fails. The stack creates only an aws.bedrock.Guardrail. There is no GuardrailVersion resource anywhere in infra/, and the stack exports `guardrail.version`, which for an unpublished guardrail is the working DRAFT (that last point comes from the provider's behaviour, not from the repo). The infra workflow writes that export into BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION. And when that variable is unset, bedrock.ts falls back to "DRAFT" in the code itself. U6b is recorded only (gated on TFA-92568, reported as Blocked): photo reading on Vertex or OpenAI, transcription on OpenAI, and text when the provider is set to openai all leave without the Bedrock guardrail. Q7 (a guardrail that intervenes never triggers the fallback) is out of scope; the code comment matches it.
Product issue (from physicianImpact): Physicians see no difference day to day. But the guardrail that masks or blocks identifiers in AI requests runs on the editable draft rather than a frozen version, so a change to the guardrail in the console takes effect at once, with no new version to review or record. Photo reading and voice transcription do not go through the guardrail at all. / A physician would see no difference. But the PII guardrail on every AI draft runs from the editable DRAFT copy, not a fixed numbered version. A later edit to the guardrail would change, without notice, what gets masked or blocked in their notes. Photos and dictation are not screened by this guardrail at all.

code-review: partial → needs a person (partial: the half that can be checked passed, the other half needs another lane / a person / a file → a person looks)
At e02167f, Quick Dictation boxes have no retention window at all: no 12, 18 or 36 h, no TTL and no timed clean-up. The only cron (apps/web/convex/crons.ts) is the hourly expired-session sweep, and convex/lib/lifecycle.ts never mentions quickDictationDrafts. A box can be deleted in only three ways, and each one is a person's action carried out on the server: (1) quickDictation.remove, called only from deleteCompartment when the physician taps delete in the Quick Dictation modal or on the sheet; (2) quickDictation.clear, which the client wires up in data/rounding.ts but never calls; (3) account deletion (account.ts), which removes boxes with via "account_deleted". Every delete writes an audit row. Assigning a box marks it and never deletes it. The pad lists every box the user owns, sorted by order, with no time filter, so the device clock never removes or hides a box from the pad. One device-clock rule exists, but it is outside the pad: the Rounding Sheet (hidden, Q14) shows an assigned box under its patient only if assignedAt falls on today's date by the device clock (compartmentsPlacedToday / isToday). The box itself stays on the pad. So the code-decidable rule passes: nothing drops a box silently. Whether boxes should clear at a set window is left to Q6, which the oracle says does not decide this verdict. Today the code would keep both boxes past T+37 h on any clock.

The snf resident record (snfFields in convex/lib/validators.ts, which convex/schema.ts spreads into snfResidents) holds name, age, dob, sex, mrn, unit and so on, but no facility. snf:add takes exactly those fields as its args, so the mutation can't accept a facility either. The Add Resident form asks only for Full Name, Date of Birth, Unit / Room and MRN, plus Encounter Type. SnfPatientCard builds its identity line from unit, dob, age and mrn. matchesPatientSearch matches on name, room, unit, mrn and diagnosis. A case-insensitive search for 'facility' under apps/web finds only prompt text, billing labels and comments, never a data field. This is exactly the recorded gap known:no-facility. As the oracle says, U4's facility part and U6's facility field are a Fail on TFA-92581, not Blocked or not-built, and that holds whatever Q1 decides about where facility comes from. retry.ts sets CALL_BUDGET_MS=30_000, RETRY_DELAY_MS=1_000, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=20_000, MIN_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=8_000 and RETRY_PRIMARY_IF_FAILED_WITHIN_MS=10_000. Each attempt's deadline is attemptTimeout(elapsed) = max(8000, min(20000, 30000 − elapsed)). chat() passes that deadline into the Bedrock invoke, which enforces it with AbortSignal.timeout. The worst path: 1. Haiku attempt 1 gets a 20 s cap but fails with a temporary error at about 9.99 s. That is under 10 s, so the retry is allowed. 2. The 1 s pause brings the clock to about 11 s. 3. Haiku attempt 2 gets max(8, min(20, 19)) = 19 s and times out at about 30 s. 4. Mistral gets max(8, min(20, 30 − 30)) = 8 s (the floor), so the sequence ends at about 38 s. Other paths stay within about 30 s: - A first failure at 10 s or more skips the retry, and the fallback gets the rest of the budget: a 20 s timeout leaves Mistral 10 s, ending at 30 s. - A "model" failure skips the retry the same way. - After a fallback earlier in the same generate, Mistral is called alone with a 20 s cap. Because of the max() the fallback never gets less than 8 s, so that part of the Then is met. The computed worst case of about 38 s is above 30 s, and that is exactly the case the oracle hands to Q22. Skipping the Haiku retry after a slow temporary failure (10 s or more) is also handed to Q22 (AC 2). No recorded gaps apply. RT-07/RT-08 are static-lane context only, and as the oracle notes, RT-08 does not model the slow-first-failure path.

All four transcript windows are hard-coded source constants in apps/web/convex/lib/lifecycle.ts, held in two `as const` objects. Dev, build e02167f, agent unit U85 (devSpec of TC-15/S04). Preset "Any urgent pending tasks?" asked once on each seeded chart (each chart: one open task flagged urgent, one open unflagged, one done). The oracle's substring checks passed (flagged task named, done task absent; Q2 record: the unflagged task was listed too), but the answer is wrong on the Nursing Home chart: it says "there are no urgent tasks documented" and lists the flagged task "Recheck weight Friday" as "routine follow-up, not time-sensitive" next to the unflagged one. Judged against U1 (each preset returns a correct, patient-specific answer; then: the answer names the flagged open task), so failed on the Nursing Home half. Hospital half: "Call ID re: blood cultures today" was called urgent and "Repeat chest X-ray tomorrow" non-urgent, which matches the flags, but only by inference from 'today' / 'tomorrow'. Cause (code reading, the review's Q2 candidate): the Ask context sends the pending tasks as text only and drops the urgent flag in both contexts (src/features/rounding/patient/askContext.ts:115-118; the Nursing Home ask uses the same builder), so the model cannot know which task the physician flagged. Also recorded for Preston (3.4): added clinical reasoning ("the blood culture follow-up is the priority to guide antibiotic therapy") and documentation-status narration. T4 (the 3.2 grade, EVALUATION_FRAMEWORK.md) belongs to TFA-94229 (in progress): todo, not judged. Rows: 2 deleted, 0 left, no other row ch…

Hospital and Nursing Home; spec newspec-c/flt-efs-s14-offline-ai.spec.ts. Network cut = context.setOffline(true) plus the Convex socket closed and every reconnect refused until the cut ends (Chromium's offline emulation alone leaves an open WebSocket working). All model answers mocked at the socket; nothing reached it while offline. Judged 36/42: 3 checks fail in each context (h2–h4, n2–n4). Pass: the banner 'No network connection. What you dictate stays on this screen and saves when you’re back online; AI steps can be retried then.' appears a few seconds after the cut; both typed lines, the Ask question and the pre-round text stay on screen; after reconnect the banner goes (~3 s) and, after one more Save Note and a reload, both encounter lines and the pre-round typed offline are on screen and on the server; one note per chart (one generateNote call). Fail (U11, state 9): 20 s after each tap while offline the step is still on its busy label — 'Generating Note…', 'Searching…', 'Saving & Updating…' — with no message on the step (only the top banner); the Convex client queues the call and the app has no timeout. Recorded (Q2): after reconnect each queued step ran by itself — the note was generated and the chart jumped to Post-Round, the question was sent (its answer went to a closed sheet), the pre-round summary was processed. Note: had the socket still looked open when the step was tapped (a real drop the browser has not noticed yet), the call would instead fail after reconnec…
Product issue: A physician who taps Generate Note & Finish, Ask AI or Save Note while the network is down sees that step's spinner ('Generating Note…', 'Searching…', 'Saving & Updating…') for the whole outage with no message on the step, only the top no-network banner. When the connection returns the step runs by itself: a note can be generated and the screen jumps to Post-Round without a new tap.

newspec-c: blocked → blocked (blocked)
Android rig: debug build of main e02167f bundled for the LOCAL stack only (bundle names 127.0.0.1:4510/4511, reached through adb reverse), built outside the checkout, on the rc_api36 emulator (Pixel 7, Android 16); Playwright attached to the app's own WebView; every ai/* action the app sends is answered or failed at the WebView's socket (no model call; aiCallLog had no new row in any run). Dictated words cannot be produced on the emulator (no microphone input, and the live transcription session must not be opened on the local stack), so TYPED text stood in for dictation, both contexts: text typed into the Hospital pre-round editor and the Nursing Home visit box stayed in the box and reached the server through a 30 s screen lock, 30 s in the background, an incoming call (the emulator's GSM console; it showed as a heads-up over the app) and 20 s of airplane mode (14/14 record-only checks). The airplane-mode 'no network' banner did NOT show here, but that is the rig: the app reaches the local stack through adb reverse, which airplane mode does not cut, and Android WebView keeps navigator.onLine true; with the app's socket really cut (EFS/S18 run) the banner shows. Generate with a 25 s model wait while the app sat 30 s in the background: the note was there on return in both contexts (gate TFA-92592: recorded). Left for a physical phone: real dictation through lock / background / a real call / airplane mode, and whether the words dictated before each interruption are kept.

Local stack on main 43c38a4f; every model call the page makes is answered in the page by ext-support.ts (an ai/* call it is not told about is failed, never forwarded) and the tripwire showed no model call. The task extractor is a rule-based stand-in that can only find what the app sends it (args.content / args.openTasks), so the app's own request, cut, merge and storage are what is judged, not the model. Spec ext-tc22-s01-s03-uat-flow.spec.ts, judged 2/4. After Save Note on the Nursing Home pre-round with 'Follow up BMP. PT eval. Recheck weight in two weeks.' the page made one model call, ai/parsing:parsePreRoundNotes, and no ai/parsing:extractTasks; Post-Round → tasks says 'No tasks yet.' / '0 pending tasks' and nothing is stored. Because no request is ever sent, no model can change this (useSnfPreRoundProcess.ts has no task call, unchanged since e02167f), so it is judged here, not on dev. Against UAT TC-22 step 4 (repeat steps 1–3 in Nursing Home), TFA-92588 AC 10 ('Pre-round tasks appear in the task list', no context named) and TFA-92592 AC 14. Open question Q3: the p72 prototype comment above TASK_SYSTEM_PROMPT says pre-round task extraction was removed by design ('at the computer you just place the order yourself'), while the Hospital pre-round on main does harvest tasks.
Product issue: Nursing Home: a physician who dictates follow-ups in the pre-round note ('Follow up BMP. PT eval. Recheck weight in two weeks.') gets no tasks at all — the task list stays 'No tasks yet.'; the Hospital pre-round with the same text makes them.

Carried from the 2026-10-14 local live-model run on e02167f (runs/2026-10-14-local/aicheck-other/extract-S07, Haiku 4.5: 17 pass, 6 fail, 6 record-only) because the code path did not change: git diff e02167f 43c38a4f is empty for the task prompts (lock hashes 22297cdb176f / 41d4bde85053 / 97468380a0ce), convex/ai/parsing.ts, providers.ts, delegatedTasks.ts, src/domain/tasks.ts, useEncounterTasks.ts and useSaveAndExtract.ts (tc22-s07-b43-codepath.txt). The computer waited 120 s with no reload: in both modes it still showed 'No note generated yet. Complete the Encounter tab first.' (Hospital also the spinning 'Finalizing Encounter Data…' button) and no note was ever stored; no failure message either. Judged U8 (UAT 3.5 / TFA-92592 AC 15): FAILED in both modes; the dictation is kept (passed). U4 / U6 (TFA-94513 in progress, TFA-94704 backlog) are todo, not judged. On 43c38a4f the note is still generated by the page: the browser calls ai/notes:generateNote, gets the text back and saves it with its own mutation (useNoteGeneration.ts finalize, snf EncounterTab.tsx handleGenerate); 'feat: use jobs for generation' (68f81eca) moved only the billing suggestion to a server job (no scheduler use for notes anywhere in convex/). The same loss is confirmed on dev with the real model (TC-14/S07 dev). Every Generate used a 'procedure-other' custom note template because on 43c38a4f saving a generated note queues a server billing job (billing/persistence.ts enqueueBilling → ai/billing.ts run) that no so…
Product issue: A physician who taps Generate on the phone and pockets it (or the app is closed) gets no note anywhere: the computer keeps showing 'No note generated yet. Complete the Encounter tab first.' and nothing says the note was lost.

(the alternative is named but not as a doubt); N-09 (dictated 'I was worried about aspiration … swallow study confirmed') → 'Cough after meals noted. Reproduced in 3 runs (no spec change after review). Device B (Honolulu, clock = server - 2 days) Save & Extract 'Hold lisinopril, BP soft.' (hold answered at the socket): stored changeDate 'Oct 11', row updatedAt and medicationsUpdatedAt 2026-10-12T07:02 (server 2026-10-14T07:02). B's screenshot 'Held · Oct 11' was taken before the server lifecycle ran; once it ran (AppLayout ContextLifecycle: whenever a page enters the Hospital section on any device, then every 10 min) it deleted the held row against its 2-day-old stamp: server medications [] and A's Medication Tracker 'No medications recorded.' Recorded only (gated TFA-94699, U20): the resident's visit date stored as B's day 'Sun Oct 11 2026'.

The tracker stamps (mergeMedEventsIntoList / useMedicationEventExtraction) use the device clock (new Date() / Date.now()). Breaks UAT 3.8 / U23 (server time; a wrong-clock device shows the same state) and TC-19 U1 (holds stay visible as open loops with their date).
